data.narrative:
Laminar, a Series A robotics and manufacturing company founded by Annie Lu and David Lu, has raised $12.4M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comparable universe of nine private and one public entity operating in robotics and manufacturing, including peers such as Humanoid, Bedrock Robotics, Dexterity, Generalist AI, and Walden Robotics.

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis, using total capital raised as a proxy baseline, applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A-to-next-stage advancement, implying a $25M valuation. Peer-median analysis examines five same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables with valuations ranging from $1.1B (Walden Robotics, Seed) to $2.0B (Generalist AI, Series B), yielding a median of $1.6B. The wide range reflects stage and maturity dispersion within the peer set.

The triangulated analysis produces a low estimate of $21M, a median of $837M, and a high of $1.9B. The substantial spread between stage-progression and peer-median results reflects genuine uncertainty around Laminar's positioning relative to more mature, later-stage robotics companies. Key uncertainties include the company's specific technology differentiation relative to Series B peers, revenue trajectory, and whether early-stage robotics valuations sustain at peer multiples. A reasonable valuation range is $100M–$500M, centering on early-stage robotics fundamentals rather than the outlier peer comparables.
